practices.practice: Read the MongoDB-compatible connection URI from an environment variable and create one process-wide MongoClient (singleton) with TLS enabled and appropriately bounded pool size and timeouts for your runtime.
practices.prior_belief: Read the MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it; use that to create a MongoClient with TLS/ssl enabled, reasonable timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS and connectTimeoutMS), and a bounded connection pool (maxPoolSize) appropriate for the app's concurrency.

practices.practice: Keep secrets out of the repository: place the DocumentDB connection URI and any LLM/embedding API keys in environment variables or a secrets store (for example, use managed identities/Entra or Key Vault) and provide only a .env.example with placeholders.
practices.prior_belief: Keep secrets out of the repo: put the DocumentDB URI and any LLM/API keys in environment variables or a secrets store (e.g., Azure Key Vault) and provide only a .env.example with placeholders in the repo.

practices.practice: Make seed operations idempotent by upserting via a deterministic key (for example name or company_id) using update/upsert or $setOnInsert so repeated runs don't create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Make seed operations idempotent by using a deterministic unique key (e.g., company_id) and upsert/replace_one with upsert=True rather than blind inserts so repeated runs don't create duplicates.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

practices.practice: For read-heavy ranking and sorting workloads, store E, S, G pillar scores as small integers and denormalize by persisting a precomputed composite (aggregate) score on each document to support fast sorting/aggregation.
practices.prior_belief: Store E, S, G scores as small integers (1-10) and store a precomputed normalized composite_score field in each document to support fast sorting/aggregation instead of recomputing in every query.

practices.practice: Store rationale text and the embedding as a numeric array field on the same document; ensure the embedding is stored as a number[] and also persist embedding model name and dimension metadata alongside the vector.
practices.prior_belief: Store the LLM rationale text and a separate embedding vector field (e.g., rationale_embedding: [float]) in the same document; keep vector field name and embedding dimension consistent across documents and persist type as float32 arrays (or BSON arrays of floats).
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector embedding storage and metadata

practices.practice: Create indexes that match your query patterns: add a unique index on an identifier (e.g., name/company_id), an index on schemaVersion, and create a descending index on any precomputed composite score or a compound index matching common filter+sort shapes to avoid blocking sorts.
practices.prior_belief: Create appropriate indexes for the queries the app runs: at minimum an index on composite_score (descending) to support ranking, plus indexes on company_id (unique) and any fields used in filters (e.g., sector); create compound indexes when queries filter+sort on multiple fields.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB indexing best practices compound index ESR

practices.practice: When using server-side vector search, create a cosmosSearch vector index on the embedding field with the chosen kind (vector-diskann/vector-hnsw/vector-ivf), the exact embedding dimension, and the similarity metric you will use at query time.
practices.prior_belief: For semantic/vector search, create a server-side vector index on the embedding field with parameters matching the index type (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN), the correct dimension, and the chosen distance metric; ensure the index's dimension matches the embedding model exactly.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index createIndexes cosmosSearch

practices.practice: If you use cosine similarity for vector search, L2-normalize embeddings at ingestion and store the embedding model name and dimensions so queries and indexes use a consistent metric and shape.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize or L2-normalize embeddings at write time if you intend to use cosine similarity with the vector index; alternatively, use whatever metric (dot/cosine/Euclidean) the index expects—do not mix metrics between stored vectors and query-time similarity.

practices.practice: Tune vector-index creation parameters (for example DiskANN lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree, HNSW m/efConstruction, IVF numLists) to balance recall and build/query cost and expect index builds to be resource-intensive; choose DiskANN for large corpora, HNSW for mid-size, and IVF for small demos.
practices.prior_belief: When creating vector indexes, include index parameters (e.g., M/efConstruction for HNSW or nlist/nprobe for IVF) tuned for production query latency/recall, and create them during a controlled maintenance window because building vector indexes can be resource-intensive.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index tuning DiskANN HNSW IVF

practices.practice: Use bulk writes (for example PyMongo bulk_write) to improve throughput when updating many documents, and handle BulkWriteError and examine upserted_ids for idempotency verification.
practices.prior_belief: Use bulk writes (bulk_write with ordered=False) when seeding many documents to improve throughput and set write concern appropriately; handle BulkWriteError and inspect result.upserted_ids for idempotency verification.
practices.how_found: Searches tried: 'Azure DocumentDB bulk_write pymongo bulk_write', 'Azure DocumentDB bulk writes best practices', 'Azure DocumentDB bulk_write guidance'; no Azure DocumentDB public page recommending bulk_write was found

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network and throttling errors (honor Retry-After when provided and handle 429/TooManyRequests), and make operations idempotent where possible.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network or rate-limit errors (handle MongoNetworkError, MongoServerSelectionError, and 429/TooManyRequests) and make operations idempotent where possible (use upserts and idempotent document updates).

practices.practice: Provision adequate cluster throughput (or enable autoscale) for your expected embedding upserts and vector-index builds and monitor normalized RU consumption and throttling (429) to scale up when needed.
practices.prior_belief: Provision database/collection throughput (RUs) or enable autoscale to support vector search and embedding-upsert workloads; monitor RU consumption and increase throughput if index builds or searches are throttled (watch for 429s).
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB autoscale and throughput guidance

practices.practice: Avoid very large documents and stay well under the service's per-document BSON size limit (plan for growth and split very large blobs into side collections), keeping vectors+text+metadata sized appropriately.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid very large documents: keep each document well under the service's per-document size limit (use referenced documents or grid storage for very large blobs) so vector fields + text + metadata don't exceed the limit.

practices.practice: Update embedding vectors and computed scores in a single document-level update (single update/upsert) to preserve atomicity and avoid inconsistent states between score and embedding.
practices.prior_belief: When updating embeddings or scores, write the embedding and composite_score in a single atomic update to avoid inconsistency between score and rationale_embedding (use single-document update/upsert to preserve atomicity).
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB single-document atomic update findAndModify

practices.practice: Store a schemaVersion and processing metadata (for example last_updated timestamp or processing_status) on each document so pipelines can resume, perform lazy migrations, and avoid reprocessing already-scored documents.
practices.prior_belief: Store a last_updated timestamp and a version or processing_status field on each document so the processing pipeline can resume, avoid reprocessing already-scored docs, and support idempotent re-run logic.

practices.practice: In aggregation pipelines, $match early to pre-filter documents before $addFields/$project, and design indexes (for example via compound ESR rule) so $sort can be covered by an index to avoid in-memory sorts; paginate using range queries rather than unbounded $skip where possible.
practices.prior_belief: Use aggregation pipeline stages efficiently: pre-filter documents in $match before $addFields/$project and use $sort with covered index on composite_score to avoid in-memory sorts; paginate with $skip/$limit or better with range queries on a sorted field.

practices.practice: Restrict network access to the cluster via firewall rules or Private Endpoint and prefer Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC or per-application least-privilege users rather than embedding account-level admin credentials in app code.
practices.prior_belief: Restrict network access to the DocumentDB cluster (firewall rules, VNet/private endpoint) and create least-privilege database users/roles for the app instead of using the account-level master key in app code.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, export metrics to Log Analytics/Azure Monitor, and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation and normalized RU consumption to detect 429 throttling and index-build impact.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument the app with diagnostics and metrics: enable Azure diagnostic logs and request/operation metrics, log slow queries and index build activity, and monitor RU usage and 429 throttling to tune indexes and throughput.

practices.practice: When using the integrated vector store, prefer storing embeddings as arrays on the same document as the source text (one vector path per document) so the server-side vector index (cosmosSearch) can index and filter by metadata in the same document.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer storing embeddings as arrays on the document rather than as separate collection documents when using server-side vector indexes, because vector indexes typically index a scalar/vector field on the same document the app queries and sorted/filtered by metadata fields.

practices.practice: For development and tests, run DocumentDB locally (Gateway Docker) or use a test database and small synthetic datasets, drive connection config via env vars, and make seed/teardown scripts idempotent to avoid polluting production throughput and data.
practices.prior_belief: In tests and development, use small synthetic datasets and a TTL index or test-only database to avoid consuming production throughput or polluting production data; make seed and teardown scripts idempotent and safe to run repeatedly.
